verdicts.explanation: The abstract and Section 2.5 give 3 mS/cm along b for hydrated RTO at room temperature after about 10 h of exposure. The value is measured in this paper by EIS, and the synthesis description matches the Methods section.

Section 2.5 states 0.28 mS/cm along b after 1 h of exposure, measured in this paper. The Introduction gives the range 0.27–3 mS/cm 'at room temperature along b', so leaving the numeric temperature null is acceptable.

field_errors.correct_value: RTO single crystal, conductivity along c after 1 h exposure (exposure time for this value not confirmed as 10 h)
field_errors.evidence: the highest conductivity is along ⃗b with 0.28 mS/cm after 1 h of exposure time to the atmosphere, which is more than two orders of magnitude than that along ⃗c, with a conductivity of 0.006 mS/cm

verdicts.explanation: The 0.006 mS/cm value sits in the sentence that frames the 1 h b-axis value, so the text ties it to 1 h exposure. The record's '10 h' label comes only from the Figure 6 caption about anisotropy, so the material's hydration state is not reliably supported.
